gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara reads as a plain sans with rounded, gappy curves and tall bowls. Bloody's round lowercase swells and bulges where the body stays uniform, so the heading looks best large and the text a size or two down.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-huninn: Commanding, a bit menacing, Bloody leads with big round bowls. Huninn follows in sans-serif strokes that look bent from steel rod, its lowercase rising close to cap height, so the swollen heading and wiry text push against each other.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-inter-tight: Big round lowercase bowls with a pronounced swell give Bloody a heavy, dripping presence on the line. Inter Tight is the sans-serif that does the quiet work, drawing flat fineliner strokes with short ascenders.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-karla: Karla is a sans with a gaping c and a tall middle band. Bloody does the shouting with its big round bowls, while Karla keeps the text stocky, modern and approachable.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-kedebideri: Loud meets friendly here. Bloody commands attention with big round bowls that swell and bulge, and Kedebideri is the sans that stays open and inviting, its tall x-height keeping the lines easy to follow.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-khula: Bloody opens with big round bowls and a commanding, slightly gruesome swagger that is hard to ignore. Khula, a sans-serif with a tall, brush-pen belly and open curves, keeps a long read comfortable.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-krub: Krub is a sans with a pronounced x-height and curves that stop before the loop closes. Bloody's big round bowls swell above it, giving the text a loud, commanding headline partner.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend: Lexend is a plain sans with outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve. And Bloody earns its keep big and short, where its round, swelling bowls can make a commanding statement.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-deca: Swollen meets smooth in this pairing. Bloody delivers the commanding, round-bowled punch of a display face, and Lexend Deca is the sans-serif that stays unshaded and approachable, its small capitals sitting beside big lowercase.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-liter: Heavy ink bulges on one side, a single thread of line on the other. Bloody's swelling round bowls are the commanding part, and Liter's sans-serif lowercase brings vertical presence.
